Update on Ohio Ballot Access Lawsuit

The article doesn't clarify why a law banning a political party from ballot was ever passed in the first place.

How does that happen?!

Well, it's not worded "We hereby ban challenger parties".

The law just looks at what challenger parties are capable of organizationally, then sets the bar a little higher than that.

For example, they threw in a bit that in addition to collecting 60k valid signatures (tons of hoops to jump through there) 500 valid signatures have to come from each of the State Senate districts. Most parties are well organized in one area, but less organized in others - pretty much only the major parties can pull this off.

Another way to do it is to pay for signatures which usually cost about $2 each with a 60% validity rate... so effectively a valid signature costs closer to $5.

Essentially having a party costs over a quarter million dollars. Pretty much nothing for the major parties - but hundreds of times the amount of money challenger parties rake in over the course of a year.

Just wanted to make myself at home with my first post to this subverse. Morrowind is a huge game full of great moments. Many of us grew up with this game and it will always be a part of our childhood. What personal memories about it will always make you remember this game?

My favorite memory is when I first saw the Telvanni mushroom houses at Tel Branora and was so confused with the place being covered in kwama eggs. Telvanni was my favorite house from then on.
What are your favorite memories from Morrowind?

I really like the Ashlands and the Ashlander tribes. I think that whole section of the main quest was one of my favorite parts of the game. The environment was harsh but also alien and kinda beautiful.

I actually only completed the main quest when I was quite a bit older from when I first played Morrowind, I've got good memories from when I was a younger child playing it, and then many years later playing it again.

I have so many memories, but there is one that sticks in my mind. I was over at a friend's place, and I had been raving about the game for weeks. I was a console player back then, so I lugged my xbox all the way to his place so he could feast on the majesty of this incredible game.

I had trouble explaining the depth of the open world aspect to him, and he wasn't convinced. I was just running around this beige looking area, fighting bugs (scrib) as far as he could see. So I said, "let's go over to this here town, there's lots going on over there." Arriving at Balmora, I walked around, told him what all these things were, and he still wasn't too convinced.

So I said, "okay, for an example... I could kill this random woman." And that's when he gets all excited. Of course, wanting to show off, but not wanting to be killed by the guards, I proceed to provoke her. After finally succeeding in convincing her to attack me, we did battle.

Now, at the time, I still hadn't figured out this game too well, so my fatigue bar was empty at the time, and I didn't realize the import of that. I also didn't realize how my skills interacted with my chance to hit. I also didn't realize Dralsea Arethi could beat me to death. So here I am, running for my life thinking it was all so crazy that this random commoner was beating the shit out of me, with all my (maybe a dozen) hours of experience. So I proceed to flee.

I run from house to house looking for shelter, when I finally decide that somehow I've lost her. Then I turn around and WHACK. I'm dead. My friend was in stitches, and so was I. Still my favorite memory. I make sure to kill her now on most playthroughs as revenge.

Perhaps not a "favorite" memory, but I will never forget about it when playing Morrowind. Early on in the main quest, you have to help some guy in the Fighter's Guild recover a Dwemmer Puzzle Cube from the nearby ruins in exchange for information. It was my first playthrough, so I had no idea where the item would be. Thus, I had explored the entire Dwemmer ruin before finally entering the side room that contained the item. I just remember being so frustrated after reaching a dead end at a pool of lava. "WHERE THE FUCK IS THIS THING??" Probably spent a good 2 hours clearing that place out, and muttering a defeated "Oh" when I found out where the item was. In subsequent playthroughs, I can just go straight to the item and be out of there in 5 minutes. I suppose the memory still makes me laugh at myself now and again..
I also looked everywhere before I found the cube. Whoever designed that dungeon must have done that on purpose to annoy as many people as possible.
Collecting all the pillows and making a fort and filling it with moon sugar.

Having played only Zelda on s/nes and one or two FF games on ps1, the first time I saw Balmora is incredible, but upon realizing the sheer size and depth of the Canton city of Vivec, I was absolutely ruined on linear games.

To this day, a linear game has to be absolutely crammed full of ridiculous, over the top, unrelenting action for me to not hate the shit out of it - and for every percent less action, there better be 5 percent more story. Literally everything (Oblivion AMD Skyrim included) pales compared to the 3000 hours I put into Morrowind, and even with that many hours, I've still never found the ring. I know I could have found it, but there was just so much to do and see, so much combat and skills to raise. I perfected "Fat Man" - a fireball spell. With Max enchantment I was able to create (out of sheer luck, trial and error, and a shit ton of mats) a full set of enchanted Daedric armor that boosted my destruction and mana to retardulous levels. Fat Man was my opus - a 136 foot wide fireball that did several hundred damage per second for like 2.7 seconds. I was already physically powerful, but I spent countless (in game) years becoming a master of destruction. I could clear a smaller cave/tomb with a single blast. I was truly a god. I know it's just a game, and it's certainly possible for a better game to be made now, but Bethesda set the bar, and even they haven't revisited it. Morrowind is my absolute best gaming experience.

What is your most popular CBD strain and what are the characteristics that make it useful?

My store currently does not carry it, but the most popular (I'm going by whats most known) is Charlotte's Web, which is a very High CBD to very Low THC ratio strain, I've heard its around a 6:1 ratio (6% CBD to 1% THC as an example) but I haven't personally seen the testing for any batch (testing varies between batches) of that strain so I'm not 100% sure on its ratio.

Other strains that tend to be very popular in the High CBD range are Harlequin (2:1 ratio) and AC/DC (not sure on the ratio).

In regards to what makes really any high CBD strain useful is the individuals use of the product. It really varies quite a bit depending on each individual and everyone has a sweet spot of THC to CBD or visa versa that works best for their needs. For instance Charlotte's Web is great for helping with seizures especially in children because it tends to have little THC leaving just the non-psychoactive CBD as the main contributor to helping reduce those seizures. So the child won't have to deal with the psycho active side effects but hopefully (cause results do vary as with anything) we see a reduction in seizures. On the other hand I've had pain management patients come in and use one of our 6:1 CBD tinctures and get "nothing from it" but the second they smoke a little high THC or eat an edible they suddenly love the 6:1 tincture in combination with something else. Its all about trial and error and finding what works best for you at this point. We are still trying to catch up on all the science.

Qualifications are still being smoothed out in the industry. With such an interest to get into it and a lot of mis-information out there knowing a lot about marijuana isn't necessarily a requirement (though knowing the right info does help). The biggest thing is knowing that it is incredibly competitive and that it is incredibly regulated (3rd most regulated industry in the US) so a lot of companies are popping up right now and trying to find ways to support the industry and are finding it hard to break in because a lot of the currently established dispensaries are not ready for those services and are afraid of taking missteps.

As long as you have a passion for the industry, have your head on straight, and know that you are getting into an industry thats not, kick you feet back and smoke a blunt, but rather faced paced hard work every day you should be fine. I suggest looking up as much info as you can that has any kind of medical backing and be skeptical of everything you read, really dig into the research so that you feel confident in what you claim the plant does. Medical Jane is a decent source as well as ProjectCBD.org, don't take everything on those websites as truth, but they are good sources to start doing a bit of research. Just remember the more you show your passion to make this industry work in a professional and legitimate way the better chance you will have of landing a job in the industry.
